title: MLX: Multi-Layer Execution for Structured LLM Workload Acceleration on Spatial Architectures
indexed_excerpt: Structured sparsity is promising for scaling LLM inference, but butterfly-structured sparse projections and transformations map inefficiently to GPUs because of deep stage dependencies and limited bulk parallelism. MLX is described as an algorithm-architecture co-design coupling semantic-aware FFT compression and hierarchical sparse projections with spatial dataflow execution, using Closed Dependency Components to fold deterministic forward-only regions across layers and pipeline compact arrays.

title: CODO: An Automated Compiler for Comprehensive Dataflow Optimization
indexed_excerpt: CODO is described as an automated compiler for FPGA dataflow accelerators that detects and eliminates coarse- and fine-grained dataflow violations, optimizes on-chip and off-chip data movement, and performs automatic scheduling for a performance-resource trade-off. title: Accelerating MoE with Dynamic In-Switch Computing on Multi-GPUs
indexed_excerpt: The indexed summary describes DySHARP, a dynamic in-switch computing solution for MoE expert parallelism. It identifies redundant inter-GPU transfers, extends static collective support with dynamic multimem addressing across ISA, architecture, and runtime, and uses token-centric kernel fusion to address asymmetric traffic reduction. The summary reports up to 1.79X speedup over a state-of-the-art solution.

title: ConServe: Contiguity-Preserving Memory Management for Multi-Turn LLM Serving
indexed_excerpt: The indexed summary describes contiguity-aware virtual-memory allocation for multi-turn LLM KV caches. ConServe reserves one contiguous virtual-address slice per conversation, maps physical pages on demand with CUDA VMM, and lazily resizes slices without copying. It identifies translation locality as a bottleneck in paged KV designs and reports lower time-to-first-token plus higher end-to-end throughput than vLLM and two vAttention variants.

title: Mapping and Communication Optimizations with Fault Tolerance for Wafer-Scale LLM Inference
indexed_excerpt: The indexed summary describes BusyBarn for fault-tolerant LLM inference on wafer-scale systems. It uses hierarchical mapping based on Transformer-block and die-array symmetry, plus Balanced Allocation with Load and Distance awareness for irregular point-to-point and multicast traffic. The summary reports up to 2.55X speedup in communication patterns and 1.08–2.14X end-to-end inference speedup.

title: HBM-CASO: A Coordinated Approach to HBM System-Level and On-Die ECC
indexed_excerpt: The indexed summary describes HBM-CASO as a protection mode that coordinates advanced system ECC with HBM on-die ECC. It reorganizes on-die ECC resources to generate a stronger on-die codeword, then uses delayed verification to accumulate on-die parity over a batch of writes before validating the batch. The summary claims broader correction of error patterns with minimal performance and bandwidth overhead.
